title: Chișinău 'empty pots' march over poverty, utility costs and government policy
location: Chișinău; reported route began at the Constitutional Court. Final route/destination differs across accounts.
scope: An actual march organized by the opposition Victory Bloc, described as a protest against government policy and poverty. Sputnik reports high utility bills and food costs and slogans against President Maia Sandu and the EU. Moldova24 says participants went toward Parliament; Sputnik says police blocked the route toward the presidential administration and the group then rallied across from the governing party office. Route disagreement retained.
organizer: Opposition Victory Bloc; Sputnik attributes remarks to Yurii Vitnyanski, Moldova24 calls him the youth bloc leader.
threshold_50_evidence: Both opened reports describe an actual march but give no attendance count. The ≥50 simultaneous threshold is unestablished.

start_date.summary: Both reports date the march to 12 October 2024.

location.summary: Both place the march in Chișinău; Sputnik identifies the Constitutional Court as the starting point, while destination accounts differ.

organizer.summary: Sputnik says the opposition Victory Bloc organized the march; Moldova24 identifies Victory Bloc youth leader Yurii Vitnyanski.

demands.summary: Sputnik links the march to high utility bills and food costs, but also records slogans against Sandu and the EU; Moldova24 describes it as a protest against government policy. Mixed cost-of-living and electoral/political messaging is retained.

participants_original.summary: Neither opened body provides an attendance figure.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Actual march is documented; simultaneous participant threshold is not.

state_response.summary: Sputnik reports police blocked the march's route toward the presidential administration; it does not describe arrests or dispersal.

protester_violence.summary: Moldova24 reports attempted provocations, but does not attribute violence to protest organizers or participants; classification remains unknown.

notes: Do not infer a participant count from photos, permits or other gatherings. Source independence between these reports is unknown. October was an election month; political slogans are retained without treating this event as purely electoral.
open_questions: Was at least 50 people present simultaneously at this march?
Can an independent contemporary account clarify the competing route/destination descriptions?
Did any demand address domestic state policy beyond the mixed cost-of-living and anti-presidential/electoral slogans?
Does this episode connect to another Victory Bloc gathering, or is it a distinct action?

title: Protest outside the Constitutional Court during referendum validation
scope: A reported public protest during the court's consideration of the 20 October referendum result. Participants included PCRM leader Vladimir Voronin and former presidential candidate Victoria Furtună, who alleged the referendum was fraudulent and challenged the process.
organizer: Not identified in the opened report.
threshold_50_evidence: Liber TV confirms an actual protest but gives no participant estimate; threshold remains unknown.

start_date.summary: Liber TV dates the gathering to 31 October 2024.

location.summary: The article places the protest outside the Constitutional Court in Chișinău.

organizer.summary: No organizer is specified; the report names Furtună and Voronin as attendees.

demands.summary: Furtună challenged referendum validation and alleged falsification, directing the grievance at the electoral process and its state adjudication.

participants_original.summary: The body names two politicians present but reports no total turnout.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Actual protest documented; no count supports ≥50.

state_response.summary: The report describes a court session and decisions but gives no protest-specific response.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is described; value remains unknown.

notes: October election/referendum context may invoke the manual's electoral-protest screening. Politicians' attendance is not turnout evidence.
open_questions: Was at least 50 people present simultaneously?
Does the manual exclude this protest as an electoral-process dispute, or does its challenge to state adjudication qualify?
Was this a new public gathering or part of another referendum protest?
